To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a domain specific modeling tool for the REA ontology that is based on the Eclipse Modelling Framework and the Eclipse Modelling Tools.

(1) we developed a REA Domain Specific Modeling Language, (2) the language is based on the UML profile metamodel and the UML profile definition framework, (3) it is based on the REA ontology as defined in [3], and (4) we have developed a graphical notation for the REA concepts
the REA DSL is (1) a domain specific modeling notation, (2) a graphical notation for REA models, and (2) a language to describe REA models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
(1) a domain specific language (DSL) to model REA models and (2) a tool support to develop, edit, and validate REA models.
the development of a domain-specific modeling language for REA models, the REA-DSL, and its corresponding tool support.
the development of a domain specific language to support the REA ontology and to enable its application for the requirements elicitation in business information systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
REA is a very useful ontology for the analysis of business and accounting phenomena.
the REASDL is a promising approach to overcome the limitations of REA in the context of enterprise modeling and enterprise information systems.
our DSL provides a solid basis for a more widespread application of REA in the field of information systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
REA DSL is a domain specific modeling approach to support the requirements elicitation in the context of accounting and enterprise systems.

REA DSL is an appropriate modeling language to support the REA based analysis of business models and to support the development of information architectures for accounting and enterprise information system.
the READSL is a language to describe business models and their information requirements in the form of a REA model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
REA can be used as the basis for the requirements elicitation of information architectures in enterprise and accounting information systems.
REA is a well suited ontology to model the requirements of accounting and enterprise systems.
the REA DSL provides a well defined and easy to understand graphical modeling language for REA concepts and their relationships.
